paper.title: Dynamic pricing and assortment under a contextual MNL demand

settings.name_in_paper: Multi-product dynamic pricing under contextual MNL demand with feature-dependent price sensitivities
unmapped: Action is a price vector for the k_t products of an adversarially chosen consideration set; customer purchases one product according to a multinomial logit model with utilities x^T theta - x^T alpha * p
Feedback is the customer's single purchase decision (categorical)
Learner knows a lower bound L on price sensitivities x^T alpha >= L
Learner knows the norm bound W on (theta, alpha) (mapped to S)
Upper bound K on consideration set size is a constant
settings.definition_quote: We consider a dynamic pricing problem for a seller with N  products represented by feature vectors $x_1,x_2,...,x_N\in \mathbb{R}^d$. In each period $t$, a customer arrives with context $z_t\in \mathbb{R}^d$ and a consideration set $S_t\subseteq [N]$, which can be chosen adversarially. For ease of notation, we consider a more general setting where customer features $z_t$ and consideration set $S_t$ are represented by $|S_t|$ adversarially chosen feature vectors $x_{t,1},...,x_{t,|S_t|}\in \mathbb{R}^d$. For all $t\in [T]$, let $k_t = |S_t|$ and let $K\leq N$ be an upper bound on $k_t$ for all $t$.

settings.name_in_paper: Single-product contextual pricing with known price coefficient and logistic noise
unmapped: Single product (k_t = 1) posted-price with binary purchase feedback under a logistic (MNL) demand model; price coefficient is a known constant
Learner knows norm bound W on theta (mapped to S)

settings.name_in_paper: MNL contextual bandits (dynamic assortment, uniform revenues)
unmapped: Reward is the MNL purchase probability of the offered assortment (multinomial logit choice model over N products with adversarial features); feedback is the single purchased item (MNL choice feedback), not independent per-item rewards
Paper's K (max assortment size) mapped to m
settings.definition_quote: In each period t, the seller observes feature vectors {x_{t,j}}_{j=1}^N ... which can be adversarially chosen. The seller needs to decide on the set S_t ⊆ [N] to offer, with |S_t| <= K. ... the customer purchases one single product j ∈ S_t ∪ {0} ... ||x_{t,j}||_2 <= 1 ... ||theta*||_2 <= W for some known constant W.

algorithms.name: Online Newton method for multiple product pricing (ONS variant with random price shocks, ONSSC)

conditions: consideration-set size bound K is constant
C depends on W, L, K (including through 1/kappa_1)

source.label: th:regret_bound_mnl
source.quote: Setting $\lambda_1 =1$, $\lambda_t = d\log(t)$ for all $t\geq 1$, there is a constant $C$ depending only on $W,L,K$ such that the regret of Algorithm \ref{alg:mnl_selfconcordant} is bounded as: $R^{\pi}(T) \leq Cd\log(T)\sqrt{T}$.

results.notes: Regret defined as expected revenue difference vs optimal prices per round. Constant C hides dependence on W, L, K and kappa_1 (possibly exponentially small). Numbering assumed Theorem 1.

conditions: price coefficient is a known constant

source.label: cor:logT
source.quote: If $k_t = 1$ for all $t$, and if the price coefficient is a known constant, then setting $\lambda_1 =1$, $\lambda_t = d\log(t)$ for all $t\geq 1$, and letting $\Delta p_{t,1} = 0$ at each step, there is a constant $C$ depending only on $W$ such that the regret of Algorithm ... is bounded as: $R^{\pi}(T) \leq Cd\log(T)$.

results.notes: Constant C depends on W (exponentially through kappa_1).

symbols.sum_kappa_star: sum_{t=1}^T kappa*_{2,t}, with kappa*_{2,t} = sum_{j in S_t*} q_{t,j}(S_t*) q_{t,0}(S_t*) <= 1
symbols.kappa_2: min over |S|<=K, j, t, ||theta||<=W of q_{t,j}(S,theta) q_{t,0}(S,theta)

conditions: constants depend only polynomially on W, not on d, K, T

source.label: th:bandit_regret
source.quote: For $\delta =\tfrac{1}{K^2T^2}$, $\lambda_1 =1,$ and $\lambda_t = d\log(tK)$ for all $t\geq 1$, the regret of Algorithm \ref{alg:OFU_MNL} satisfies, for some constants $\Tilde{C_1}$ and $\Tilde{C_2}$ that do not depend on $d,K,T$ and that depend only polynomially on $W$: R(T) \leq \Tilde{C_1}Kd\log(KT)(\sqrt{\sum_{t=1}^T \kappa^*_{2,t}}) + \frac{\Tilde{C_2}d^2K^4}{\kappa_2}\log(KT)^2.

results.notes: Paper's K (assortment size) mapped to m. Theorem states K^4 in second term while the proof derives K^3; recorded as stated. Regret defined via expected purchase probabilities (pseudo-regret). Algorithm noted as computationally expensive.
